chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَ سَعِيدٌ الْأَعْرَجُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ :

translations.en: Saʿīd al-Aʿraj asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: عَنْ قِدْرٍ فِيهَا لَحْمُ جَزُورٍ وَقَعَ فِيهَا أُوقِيَّةٌ مِنْ دَمٍ أَيُؤْكَلُ مِنْهَا

translations.en: about a pot in which there was camel meat, and an ounce of blood fell into it: may one eat from it?
He said: "Yes, for the fire consumes the blood."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a pot of camel meat into which a measure of blood has fallen. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام permits eating from it, explaining that the fire consumes the blood during cooking.
en.seo_question: Can meat be eaten if blood falls into the cooking pot?

key_terms.أُوقِيَّةٌ: a measured amount, here an ounce
key_terms.دَمٍ: blood that fell into the pot
key_terms.تَأْكُلُ: consumes or eliminates in the context of cooking
